facts.statement: Malawisaurus fossils are found in the Dinosaur Beds of northern Malawi, dating to the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It is known from the Dinosaur Beds of northern Malawi, which probably date to the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Sidney H. Haughton originally described Malawisaurus dixeyi in 1928 as a species of Gigantosaurus.
facts.quote: Malawisaurus dixeyi was originally described in 1928 by Sidney H. Haughton as a species of Gigantosaurus

facts.statement: Louis L. Jacobs and colleagues renamed the species Malawisaurus in 1993 based on new material.
facts.quote: In 1993 it was placed in the newly named genus Malawisaurus by Louis L. Jacobs and colleagues, based on newly collected material from the locality.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is a partial skeleton identified as SAM 7405 from the Mwakasyunguti locality.
facts.quote: The holotype is SAM 7405, a partial skeleton and its type locality is Mwakasyunguti.

facts.statement: Malawisaurus lived approximately 116 million years ago during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 116 millones de años, en el Aptiense, en lo que hoy es África.

facts.statement: Malawisaurus was relatively small for a sauropod, reaching lengths of about 15 meters and weighing about 10 tonnes.
facts.quote: Relatively small by sauropod standards, Malawisaurus reached lengths of about 15 m, and weighed about 10 t.

facts.statement: A 2020 study estimated Malawisaurus to be about 11 meters long and weigh 2.8 tonnes.
facts.quote: In 2020 it was given a smaller estimation of 11 meters (36 ft) and 2.8 tonnes (3.1 short tons).

facts.statement: Malawisaurus is one of the few titanosaurids for which skull material has been found.
facts.quote: Es uno de los pocos titanosáuridos para los cuales se ha encontrado el material del cráneo.

facts.statement: By definition, Malawisaurus is the most basal lithostrotian.
facts.quote: By definition, Malawisaurus has to be the most basal lithostrotian.

facts.statement: The time range for Malawisaurus is estimated between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: While the Dinosaur Beds are usually considered Barremian-Aptian, some researchers suggest they might be Late Cretaceous based on the vertebrate assemblage.
facts.quote: though they have also been suggested to be Late Cretaceous in age based on the vertebrate assemblage.

facts.statement: Malawisaurus is related to the Brazilian dinosaur Gondwanatitan, which was a member of the Aeolosaurini.
facts.quote: Está relacionado con el Gondwanatitán de Brasil, que fue un miembro del Aeolosaurini.

rejected.statement: Malawisaurus is an extinct genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur.
rejected.quote: Malawisaurus (meaning "Malawi lizard") is an extinct genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'is an extinct genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur'

rejected.statement: Ossicles found on Malawisaurus are believed to represent dermal scutes that covered its skin.
rejected.quote: Like some other titanosaurs, ossicles have been found which are believed to represent dermal scutes that covered the skin.
